facts.fact_text: On 26 February 2003 at 8 a.m. the applicant was visited at home by two police officers from the Shengavit District Police Department (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Շենգավիթի բաժին).
The applicant was taken to the Shengavit District Police Department police station on 26 February 2003.
At the Shengavit District Police Department police station an administrative case was initiated against the applicant.
The applicant was charged under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – the Code of Administrative Offences) with minor hooliganism.
The charge of minor hooliganism against the applicant was on the ground that he had participated in the unauthorised demonstration of 23 February 2003 and had violated public order.
Judge H. found the applicant guilty as charged under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences with minor hooliganism.
Judge H. sentenced the applicant to ten days of administrative detention.
Judge H. found that on 23 February 2003 on Mashtots Avenue in Yerevan the applicant participated together with a group of people in an unauthorised demonstration and march, and violated public order.
The applicant was taken to a detention facility to serve his ten-day sentence of administrative detention.
The applicant was charged under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք – the Code of Administrative Offences) with minor hooliganism.
The charge of minor hooliganism against the applicant was on the ground that he had participated in the unauthorised demonstration of 23 February 2003 and had violated public order.
Judge H. found that on 23 February 2003 on Mashtots Avenue in Yerevan the applicant participated together with a group of people in an unauthorised demonstration and march, and violated public order.
The decision of Judge H. of 26 February 2003 stated that it could be protested against by the prosecutor under Article 289 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

By a letter of 11 April 2003 the Ministry of Justice informed the applicant that the rights of persons charged with an administrative offence were defined in Article 276 of the Code of Administrative Offences and should have been invoked by the applicant during the examination of his case.
The Ministry of Justice's letter of 11 April 2003 further stated that the decision of 26 February 2003 could be protested against by the prosecutor.

Judge H. found that on 23 February 2003 on Mashtots Avenue in Yerevan the applicant participated together with a group of people in an unauthorised demonstration and march, and violated public order.

The President of the Criminal and Military Court of Appeal found, in reviewing the applicant's conviction, that the applicant had been subjected to administrative detention for attending an unauthorised demonstration in the Kentron District of Yerevan on 23 February 2003 and violating public order, according to the decision of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan.

The President of the Criminal and Military Court of Appeal found, having reviewed the applicant's appeal and the materials concerning the administrative offence, that the penalty imposed on the applicant must be changed.

On 26 March 2003 the applicant sent an application to the Ministry of Justice (ՀՀ արդարադատության նախարարություն) arguing that he had never participated in any demonstrations, and in particular the one held on 23 February 2003, and seeking a review of his case.

On 26 March 2003 the applicant sent an application to the Court of Cassation (ՀՀ վճռաբեկ դատարան) arguing that he had never participated in any demonstrations, and in particular the one held on 23 February 2003, and seeking a review of his case.

On 26 March 2003 the applicant sent an application to the Presidential Human Rights Commission (ՀՀ նախագահին առընթեր մարդու իրավունքների հարցերի հանձնաժողով) arguing that he had never participated in any demonstrations, and in particular the one held on 23 February 2003, and seeking a review of his case.

By a letter of 16 April 2003 the President of the Criminal and Military Court of Appeal informed the applicant that his application of 26 March 2003 could not be examined, since the applicant had missed the prescribed 10-day time-limit for appeal.

By a letter of 17 April 2003 the General Prosecutor's Office gave a reply to the applicant's application addressed to the Presidential Human Rights Commission similar to the reply given by the President of the Criminal and Military Court of Appeal on 16 April 2003.
By a letter of 6 May 2003 the Ministry of Justice gave the same reply as its letter of 11 April 2003 in response to the applicant's complaint of 27 April 2003.
